match.reason: The bank point defines entrepreneurs, risk and innovation and says nothing about government or community support such as research funding, council grants, school programs or start-up hubs, which is what the new point teaches.

draft.title: Encouraging innovation in a nation
card: Innovation means new ideas, products or ways of working. A nation gains when many people try new ideas and start businesses.
Research funding
governments pay for research, for example at universities, so new knowledge can lead to new products and businesses.
Council grants
local councils give money to small and new businesses, which helps them cover early costs.
School programs
programs in entrepreneurship teach students how to turn ideas into businesses. Regional start-up hubs give new businesses in country areas shared space, advice and contacts.
draft.remember: Funding, grants, school programs and hubs all make it easier to turn new ideas into businesses.

a.q: A council gives a small amount of money to new local businesses to help with their first costs. Which type of support is this?
a.why: Money from a local council to new businesses is a council grant. Research funding is also money, but it is paid for research such as at universities, not to new businesses for early costs.
a.clue: Think about who is giving the money and who receives it.

b.q: Hana lives in a country town in Victoria. She wants to start an app business but has no office, no advice and no contacts. Which support would suit her need best?
opts: A regional start-up hub in her area
Research funding paid to a university
A council grant paid to an older business
b.why: A regional start-up hub gives shared space, advice and contacts to new businesses in country areas, which matches what Hana lacks. A school program teaches students about starting businesses but does not give her space or contacts.
b.clue: Which support offers space, advice and contacts together?

b.best: A regional start-up hub in her area

The repeated word gives the answer away without testing whether students know what a grant is. Describe the giver differently, for example 'the local shire', or test the idea through a scenario.
